text:
A building of three floors was destroyed by fire early this morning at Wing Lok Street, which was the scene of a similar occurrence soon after the big Hotel Fire on New Year's Day.
The structure was one measuring 45 x 14 feet. The ground floor was occupied by Shan Fat, a dealer in birds' nest and Chinese provisions. The first floor was used by the Lee Yuen Loong medicine shop. The upper floor formed the class rooms of the Kwok Kwok School.

label: text
text: The fire is believed to have had its origin in the cockloft of the provision store on the ground floor and to have rapidly worked upwards after it had secured a hold on the staircases.

label: text
text: There were a few Chinese sleeping on the premises, mostly on the first floor, and they were reused from their slumbers when the building was well alight. They made their escape by scaling along the verandah into the next building. Bamboo scaffolding put up for repairs here-assisted the men in reaching safety.

label: text
text: Central Fire Station received first news of the outbreak at 3:44 this morning through the patent fire alarm at Wing Lok Street, and simultaneously with the departure of two engines from here appliances were also called up from Kennedy Town and Wan-

label: text
text: On arrival it was found that the ground and first floors were well alight and the upper floor had also been taken in by the spreading flames. Two motor pumps were brought to work and hoses directed from the verandahs of the building opposite yielded effective results. The sea was also tapped and a hose was drawn up to the roof of the house adjoining the burning building. A good jet was thrown on the flames from this vantage point. The stop signal was given after 29 minutes' strenuous work by the fire-fighters.

label: text
text:
The damage as far as the building is concerned has not been assessed, and it is not known whether it is covered by insurance. The roof and upper floor were completely burnt out. The first floor was also badly damaged by fire, but did not actually collapse. However, there was very little left of it.
The provision dealer lost practically all his stock through damage by both fire and water. The contents of the first floor were also destroyed. It is understood that the stock in both these floors was insured with the Phoenix and other insurance companies for a total of $12,000.

label: text
text: Having sold property on the security of which he had lent $25,000, the mortgagor was still $11,119.50 short and this morning, in the Supreme Court, claimed through Mr. Elsley Zeitlyn, the balance.

label: text
text: The property concerned was in Elgin Street, Hongkong. Ng King-po was the plaintiff and Ip Chu, the defendant, the latter not being represented.

label: text
text:
Plaintiff gave evidence of having advanced the money for six months, interest to be $10 per $1,000 per month. A clear month was to be given for the calling in of principal and interest. Notice was given on May 18, 1925, asking for payment by June 28. To this no reply had been received. On June 29 another notice had been sent together with an intimation that the property would be sold within a month if the money was not paid. In August, the property was sold to the highest bidder.
Mr. H. K. Woo, plaintiff's solicitor, gave evidence of the drafting and delivery of these letters.

text: Local "Lans" (wholesale depots) commission stevedores to take delivery of live pigs, consigned to them, on the arrival of incoming steamers. Those who bring in the first lot from a ship get an extra thirty events per pig, as the loss landed earlier command the best sale.

As the "Chinhua" was entering hairboard about 10 p.m. on Sunday two sampans, both showing flares, tried to make fast while she was, under way, near "Green Island."
Words passed in Chinese. It is believed that those in the sampans learned that the ship (coming from Bangkok, via Hoihow) had no pigs on board.

label: text
text:
One of the sampans got in the way. There was a collision, sternly to stern end on. The sampam became a total wreck. A boat was put off in very quick time from the "Chinaia" in charge of a European officer but according to the statement of those on the other sampam the occupants of the damaged boat had been picked up.
After it had been ascertained that there was nobody else in the water, the steamer proceeded.
In this morning's vernacular papers it is stated that one of the stavedores has not been accounted for.

text: An agreement has been reached along broad lines for the funding of the Italian debt.

label: text
text: The drafting Committee meets to-morrow to settle the points in detail.

label: text
text: Both sides are silent on the terms of the British-Italian debt settlement.

label: text
text: Count Volpi, interviewed by Reuter, admitted that an agreement had been reached on fundamental points, but tactfully evaded the question whether the agreement was satisfactory to Italy and also how it compared with the American settlement, but well-informed circles are of opinion that annuities of four and a half million sterling will begin to be paid immediately.

label: text

label: text

label: text
text: A drafting committee will meet to-morrow morning, and a further meeting of the Ministers will take place in the afternoon. There is every confidence, says the communiqué, that an agreement will be reached.

label: text
text: At the meeting between representatives of the railway companies and of the National Union of Railwaymen, which was held this morning, there was a full discussion of the objections raised by the men to the award of the National Wages Board. As explained in previous messages the men object to the finding of the National Wages Board that men hereafter joining the railway service and not promoted shall receive only the basic wage of those grades to which they are appointed without cost of living bonus, and they ask for an assurance that the railway companies will accept the basic rates as an irreducible minimum. The exact tenor of the railway companies' reply has not been announced.

label: text
text: At a conference of railway-men's delegates this afternoon two resolutions were moved. One resolution was for refusing to accept the award and declaring a strike next Friday. The other was for acceptance of the award. By a very narrow majority the resolution accepting the award was adopted. It would appear therefore that the railway crisis is over.

label: text
text:
London, Jan. 25.
Critical negotiations between representatives of the railway companies and the N.U.R. were opened at Euston this morning in regard to the Union's demands.
Several Branches of the Union have already adopted a resolution in favour of a national strike if the Union's demands are refused.
At the conclusion of the negotiations the companies submitted a memorandum which the delegates' conference of railwaymen will consider.

label: text
text: At to-day's negotiations the railway companies declined to concede the points raised by the Railwaymen's Union. They pointed out that they accepted the findings of the Wages Board, which the Union repudiated a second time after the Union's representatives had signed the report. The companies intimated that if the Union persisted in this attitude they would be out-aged seriously to consider their attitude toward the Wages Board machinery which was being rendered "futile and farcical."

label: text
text: Passionate speeches were delivered on both sides at the railwaymen's conference in debating the motion for a definite strike on Friday, which was ultimately rejected by 41 votes to 36. The outcome is regarded as a triumph for Mr. J. H. Thomas, who throughout strove to unhold the prestige of the Wages Board.

Lord Revelstoke, the well-known banker, in proposing the health of Count Volpi, expressed the conviction that the negotiations on which his Excellency was engaged would result in strengthening and cementing the friendship and amity which for so many generations had united Great Britain and Italy.
Count Volpi, replying, said that he could not tell what would be the conclusion of his conversations with the British Chancellor of the Exchequer, but the outcome could not be other than a fair and mutual recognition of their respective actual situations, illuminated by the traditional friendship between two countries.

label: text
text:
The rumour that a Chinese had been arrested in connection with the big burglary at the Popular Silk Store, a full report of which appeared in the "China Mail" yesterday, was confirmed on inquiry in official circles this morning. It is understood, however, that the man had been arrested on suspicion and no developments have eventuated.
Further inquiries show that the thieves effected an easy entrance to the first floor. In the majority of local burglaries it is generally accepted that where it is difficult to gain access to an upper floor the thieves throw a bamboo pole near the place planned for the burglary during daylight and climb along this in the night hours. In the present instance the first floor where the thieves dug through was vacant and it had remained so for a long time. A staircase at the back of the building gave free access to the room which had once been used as a fitting room.

label: text
text:
It was also to facilitate access direct from the ground floor that Madame Flint, before she vacated the shop, now occupied by the Popular Silk Store, put in a staircase from the attic. Allowance was made for this when the floor was put in and no concrete or expanded metal was used on this part. The opening had been closed in with planks and mortar. Knowing the weak part in the floor the thieves found no difficulty in boring through.
The theory is advanced that the thieves were the same or part of the gang that carried out a series of during burglaries from a European and two Chinese stores one year ago.

label: text
text: A claim respecting an admittedly illegal firm was heard in the Summary Court this morning.

label: text
text: Under the local Ordinance, a firm is not entitled to the status of legal recognition if it has more than twenty partners and in the particular case in question there were more than this number.

label: text
text: The firm was formed for the purpose of building a house at Swatow and the partners were called upon to pay sums averaging $1,000 each.

label: text
text: The only two partners who appeared in court this morning said that they had seen nothing further of their capital or interest. The scheme had gone forward and the house had, in fact, been built. A witness in giving evidence said that he had looked after the hocks and there had been $8,000 profit which had been handed to the defendant who had sponsored the scheme.

label: text
text: Plaintiff (represented by Dr. D. McCallum) "claimed for the return of the money he had invested"

label: text
text:
Mr. J. A. Gordon Leask held that as the firm was an illegal one there was no legal responsibility for the return of the money invested even if the scheme for which it was formed had gone through. He further held that plaintiff should be non-suited as he held that His Worship had no jurisdiction in such a case.
Judgment was reserved.

label: text
text: The campaign of the Canton Government against Chan Kwingming's remnants in the south of Kwantang province and the island of Hainan is now almost complete.

label: text
text: A description of how, after crossing the Hainan Straits, the Canton forces took the island is given below.

label: text
text: The Cantonese soldiers that landed in Hainan on Sunday night (Jan. 17) arrived in Kiungchow and Hoihow this afternoon. There had been very little fighting as the local men, although having twice as many soldiers, were not trained and put up the white flag as soon as they made a start at fighting. On Wednesday (Jan. 20) the local officials heard that their "braves" were surrendering and that the Cantonese were having a triumphal march to Kiungchow and Hoihow. General Tang Punyan and his assistants were greatly put out and decided that the best thing for them was to get out as fast as possible. This they decided to do and during the night they all faded away. This morning there was not an officer to be seen and it was not long before there were no soldiers. The exit was so sudden that many guns and much ammunition were left in the house above the city gate that had been occupied by soldiers. The ammunition factory worked up till last night but it is said that not even bed-boards were left this morning. Some soldiers wanted to give their arms to foreigners in Hoihow, and when the offer was refused, threw them into the river. There was a little looting in a few shops in Kiungchow on Wednesday night but the turnover was so sudden that the local thieves did not even have a chance. There was scarcely any looting in Hoihow.

label: text
text: The Cantonese troops presented a very good appearance and behaved very well as they entered Kiungchow and Hoihow. The local people, from past experience, feared that the in-coming troops would loot and many women and children left the city to seek refuge. They were soon able to return to their homes in peace for the new soldiers scattered handbills saying that they had come to save Hainan from their oppressors and that they would not take anything they did not pay for and that the people had nothing to fear. The men were as good as their word and did not enter private houses but paid for everything they needed. I hear that proclamations have been posted forbidding gambling and opium smoking and promising that no unjust taxes will be raised. The banners of the soldiers stated that they were the anti-imperialists and the posters said that they had come to fight Tang, "the tool of foreign imperialists." It is to be hoped now that they are in power they will attempt to put down the bandits and give peace and justice to the people of Hainan. There are several Russians in the army and quite a number of Hainanese students.

label: text
text: It is reported that the Custom's houseboat was coming in from the Japanese warship with a guard of Japanese soldiers when the new Cantonese soldiers stopped the boat. They disarmed the Japanese but their guns were afterwards returned to them and I suppose the incident closed.

label: text
text: No word has been received from the interior but it will not be many days before the entire island is in the control of the invaders. It remains to be seen what will be the attitude of the government towards trade with Hongkong. Some do not expect as much trouble as in Canton for there are no factories here and the labour unions are not very active.
